chapters.name: Catching crabs New words

words.ex: The preceding chapter explains the basics.
words.ex_cn: 前一章解释了基础知识。
words.en: Existing or coming before something else in time, order, or importance.

words.ex: He starts his new class in the fall semester.
words.ex_cn: 他在秋季学期开始他的新课程。
words.en: A semester is one of the two periods that the school or college year is divided into, especially in the United States and Canada.

words.tr:
adj. 无准备的；即兴的；即席的
adv. 无准备地；即兴地；即席地
words.ex: He gave an impromptu speech at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在派对上做了一次即兴演讲。
words.en: An impromptu action is one that you do without planning or organizing it in advance.

words.tr:
n. 划船；泛舟
v. 划船；用船运输；用船装运；“boat”的现在分词
words.ex: They enjoy boating on the lake every weekend.
words.ex_cn: 他们每个周末都喜欢在湖上划船。
words.en: Boating is the activity of traveling in a boat for pleasure.

words.ex: His attendance at the meeting was mandatory.
words.ex_cn: 他必须出席这次会议。
words.en: The act of being present at a place or event.

words.ex: The road rises steeply up the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 这条路大坡度地向上延伸到山上。
words.en: In a manner that is steep; sharply or abruptly.

words.ex: He felt humiliation after failing the test in front of everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他在大家面前考试失败后感到羞辱。
words.en: Humiliation is the embarrassment and shame you feel when someone makes you appear stupid, or when you make a mistake in public.

words.ex: He shows diligence in doing his homework every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天认真完成作业。
words.en: Conscientiousness in paying proper attention to a task; giving the degree of care required in a given situation.

words.ex: He handed out a flyer about the concert.
words.ex_cn: 他分发了一张关于音乐会的传单。
words.en: A flyer is a small handbill advertising an event or product.

words.ex: He wrote a script for a short movie.
words.ex_cn: 他为一部短片写了剧本。
words.en: A script is the written form of a play, film, or broadcast. It includes the dialogue and stage directions.

words.ex: He took a provisional job until he found a better one.
words.ex_cn: 他在找到更好的工作之前做了一份临时工作。
words.en: Something that is provisional is temporary and likely to be changed or replaced in the future.

words.ex: His acceptance of the offer made everyone happy.
words.ex_cn: 他接受了这份提议，让大家都很高兴。
words.en: The act of agreeing to receive or undertake something offered.

words.ex: He is an ambitious student who wants to become a doctor.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个有雄心的学生，想成为一名医生。
words.en: Having or showing a strong desire and determination to succeed.

words.ex: He is an activist who helps the poor.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位帮助穷人的积极分子。
words.en: An activist is a person who works to bring about political or social change by campaigning, public speaking, or demonstrating.

words.tr: n. 代表大会；议会；国会；
words.ex: The congress met to discuss new laws.
words.ex_cn: 代表大会召开以讨论新法律。
words.en: A congress is a formal meeting of representatives, as of various nations, to discuss problems or to make decisions.

words.ex: He took out a mortgage to buy his first house.
words.ex_cn: 他申请了一笔抵押贷款来购买他的第一套房子。
words.en: A mortgage is a loan of money which you get from a bank or building society in order to buy a house.

words.ex: The new policy is for the promotion of clean energy.
words.ex_cn: 这项新政策是为了促进清洁能源。
words.en: A promotion is a move to a more important job or rank in a company or organization.

words.ex: He will inevitably fail if he doesn't study.
words.ex_cn: 如果他不学习，他不可避免地会失败。
words.en: If something will inevitably happen, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.ex: He often criticizes his brother for being late.
words.ex_cn: 他经常批评他弟弟迟到。
words.en: If you criticize someone or something, you express your disapproval of them by saying what you think is wrong with them.

words.tr:
n. 支撑物；支架；牙箍
v. 支撑；绷紧；紧靠；准备好
words.ex: The old bookshelf needs a brace to stay steady.
words.ex_cn: 旧书架需要一个支撑物来保持稳定。
words.en: To brace oneself means to prepare oneself for something difficult or unpleasant.

words.ex: The people showed resistance against the unfair law.
words.ex_cn: 人们对这项不公平的法律表示抵抗。
words.en: Resistance is the refusal to accept or comply with something; the attempt to prevent something by action or argument.

words.tr:
n. 旷野地；荒野；高沼
v. （使）停泊；系泊
words.ex: The sheep graze on the moor near the village.
words.ex_cn: 羊在村庄附近的旷野地上吃草。
words.en: A moor is an area of open land, often with poor soil, that is covered with grass, heather, and low bushes. It can also refer to the act of securing a ship or boat to a fixed object or the land.

words.tr: n. 港湾；河口湾；河口；入海口；
words.ex: The river flows into the estuary before reaching the sea.
words.ex_cn: 河流在入海前流入港湾。
words.en: An estuary is the wide part of a river where it nears the sea; fresh and salt water mix.

words.ex: The boat travels along the coastline.
words.ex_cn: 船沿着海岸线航行。
words.en: The coastline is the outline of a coast, especially its shape and appearance.

words.tr:
n. 激浪；拍岸浪花；
v. 冲浪；（互联网上）冲浪；
words.ex: He bought a new surf for the beach trip.
words.ex_cn: 他为海滩之旅买了一块新的激浪。
words.en: To surf means to ride on the crest of a wave towards the shore, typically on a surfboard. It can also mean to browse the internet.

words.ex: The coastal village has beautiful beaches.
words.ex_cn: 这个沿海村庄有美丽的海滩。
words.en: relating to the coast, the area where the land meets the sea

words.ex: The old bike has a rusty chain.
words.ex_cn: 这辆旧自行车的链条生锈了。
words.en: If something is rusty, it is covered with rust or has become less good because it has not been used for a long time.

words.ex: The net is made of a fine mesh.
words.ex_cn: 这个网是由细密的网状物制成的。
words.en: A mesh is a material made of a network of wire or thread to catch or hold things, or to allow things to pass through it.

words.tr:
v. 拖；拉；拖运；
n. 拖；拉；拖运；
words.ex: He hauled the heavy box across the room.
words.ex_cn: 他把沉重的箱子拖过了房间。
words.en: To haul something means to pull it or carry it with a lot of effort.

words.ex: The children played on the deck of the ship.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在船的甲板上玩耍。
words.en: A deck is a floor-like surface on a ship, or a set of cards used in games. It can also mean to decorate or adorn something.

words.tr:
n. 边；边缘；帽边
v. （装）满；（使）溢出
words.ex: The cup is full to the brim.
words.ex_cn: 杯子装得满满的。
words.en: The top edge of a container or the projecting edge of a hat.

words.ex: He used a clamp to hold the wood together.
words.ex_cn: 他用夹具把木头固定在一起。
words.en: A clamp is a device that holds two things firmly together. As a verb, to clamp means to hold or fasten something tightly.

words.ex: The boy defied his parents by staying out late.
words.ex_cn: 这个男孩因为熬夜不回家而违抗了父母。
words.en: If you defy someone or something, you refuse to obey them or you do something that they do not allow.

words.ex: The captive man sat quietly in his cell.
words.ex_cn: 那个被监禁的人安静地坐在牢房里。
words.en: A captive is someone who is being kept as a prisoner or in a confined space, or something that is held or confined.

words.tr: adj. 富有成效的；多产的；生产的；
words.ex: He had a productive day and finished all his work.
words.ex_cn: 他度过了富有成效的一天，完成了所有工作。
words.en: Producing or able to produce large amounts of goods, crops, or other commodities.

chapters.name: Catching crabs Phrases and expressions

words.w: at the back of one's mind
words.tr: 短语. 在某人潜意识里；某人心中隐隐约约地想着的
words.uk: æt ðə bæk əv wʌnz maɪnd
words.us: æt ðə bæk əv wʌnz maɪnd
words.ex: There is a worry at the back of his mind about the test.
words.ex_cn: 他对考试有一丝隐隐的担忧。
words.en: If something is at the back of your mind, you are aware of it but it is not your main thought or concern at the moment.

words.w: in the back of one's mind
words.tr: phrase. 在内心深处；潜意识里；隐约记得
words.uk: ɪn ðə bæk əv wʌnz maɪnd
words.us: ɪn ðə bæk əv wʌnz maɪnd
words.ex: He always has a worry in the back of his mind.
words.ex_cn: 他心里总是有个担忧挥之不去。
words.en: If something is in the back of your mind, you are aware of it but it is not your main thought or concern at the moment.

words.tr: phrase. 详细规划；制定；筹划；在地图上标出路线
words.ex: He will map out the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会规划出这个计划。
words.en: To plan or arrange something in detail.

words.tr: phrase. 结束；告终；意外到达
words.ex: He didn't plan to stay, but he ended up sleeping there.
words.ex_cn: 他本没打算留下，但最后在那里睡了。
words.en: If you end up in a particular place or situation, you are in that place or situation after a series of events, even though you did not originally intend to be.

words.tr: 短语. 想要做某事；正打算做某事
words.ex: She is looking to do something adventurous this summer.
words.ex_cn: 她这个夏天想要做一些冒险的事情。
words.en: If you are looking to do something, you are intending or planning to do it.

words.tr: phrase. 定居；平静下来；专心于
words.ex: He wants to settle down with a family.
words.ex_cn: 他想安定下来组建家庭。
words.en: To settle down means to start living in a place where you intend to stay for a long time, usually after moving around a lot.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 把……拖起；拉起；举升
words.ex: They haul up the boat onto the shore.
words.ex_cn: 他们把船拖上岸。
words.en: To pull or drag something or someone up, especially with effort.

words.tr: phrase. 算出；弄明白；解决；想出
words.ex: I can't figure out the answer.
words.ex_cn: 我算不出答案。
words.en: To understand or solve something by thinking about it.

chapters.name: We are all dying New words

words.ex: The bearer of the ticket can enter the concert.
words.ex_cn: 票的持有人可以进入音乐会。
words.en: A bearer is someone who carries or holds something, especially a document or message, or someone who is entitled to receive something, such as a check or a ticket.

words.tr:
v. 成为三倍；使增至三倍；
n. 三倍的数；三个一组；
adj. 三部分的；
words.ex: The company's profits tripled last year.
words.ex_cn: 该公司去年的利润增长了三倍。
words.en: To triple something means to make it three times as much in size or number.

words.ex: He needs to substantiate his claim with evidence.
words.ex_cn: 他需要用证据来证实他的说法。
words.en: To substantiate a statement or a story means to supply evidence which proves that it is true.

words.ex: He saw a wooden coffin at the funeral.
words.ex_cn: 他在葬礼上看到一个木制棺材。
words.en: A coffin is a box in which a dead body is buried or cremated.

words.ex: The cave dweller lives alone in the mountain.
words.ex_cn: 洞穴居民独自住在山里。
words.en: A dweller is a person or animal that lives in or at a specified place.

words.ex: The cows trample the grass in the field.
words.ex_cn: 牛在田野里践踏草地。
words.en: If someone tramples something or tramples on it, they step heavily and carelessly on it and damage it.

words.ex: The old cemetery is near the church.
words.ex_cn: 那个古老的墓地在教堂附近。
words.en: A cemetery is a place where dead people are buried.

words.tr: adj. 戴头巾的；有罩盖的
words.ex: The hooded figure slipped into the shadows.
words.ex_cn: 那个戴头巾的身影悄悄溜进了阴影中。
words.en: Having a hood or resembling a hood.

words.ex: He pulled the hood over his head to stay dry.
words.ex_cn: 他把兜帽拉到头上以保持干燥。
words.en: A hood is a part of a coat or jacket that you can pull up to cover your head.

words.tr:
n. 长柄大镰刀
v. 用长柄大镰刀割
words.ex: The farmer swings the scythe to cut grass.
words.ex_cn: 农夫挥动镰刀割草。
words.en: A scythe is a tool with a long curved blade at right angles to a long handle, used for cutting grass, grain, or other crops.

words.ex: He works as a teacher but his sideline is selling handmade crafts.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名教师，但他的副业是卖手工制品。
words.en: A sideline is an activity that you do in addition to your main job in order to earn extra money.

words.ex: There is uncertainty about the weather tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天的天气还不确定。
words.en: Uncertainty is a situation in which something is not known, or something that is not known or certain.

words.tr: n. 虚弱；衰弱；（性格或道德上的）弱点
words.ex: His frailty made it hard to walk far.
words.ex_cn: 他的虚弱让他难以走远路。
words.en: Frailty is the condition of being weak and delicate.

words.tr: adj. 不合时宜的；过早发生的
words.ex: His untimely death shocked everyone.
words.ex_cn: 他突如其来的去世让所有人都感到震惊。
words.en: If you describe an event as untimely, you mean that it happened earlier than it should, or sooner than you expected.

words.ex: The dark forest looks scary at night.
words.ex_cn: 这个黑暗的森林在晚上看起来吓人。
words.en: If something is scary, it causes fear or alarm.

words.tr: adj. 开始发育（发展）的；初露头角的； v. “bud”的现在分词；
words.ex: He is a budding artist who loves to paint.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位刚开始发展艺术才能的画家。
words.en: A budding artist, writer, etc. is someone who is starting to show skill or talent in that area.

words.tr: n. 土窖；地穴；教堂地下室
words.ex: He found a crypt under the old church.
words.ex_cn: 他在旧教堂下面发现了一个地窖。
words.en: A crypt is a room or chamber beneath a church, used as a burial place.

words.tr: n. 踢者；善踢的人；爱踢的马；抱怨者
words.ex: The kicker scored the winning goal in the last minute of the game.
words.ex_cn: 这位踢球者在比赛的最后一分钟踢进了制胜一球。
words.en: A kicker is someone who kicks something, especially a football player who kicks the ball during a game. It can also refer to an unexpected or surprising ending to a story or situation.

words.ex: The book begins with a short prologue.
words.ex_cn: 这本书以一个简短的序言开始。
words.en: A prologue is an introduction to a book, play, or other written work that sets the scene or provides background information.

words.ex: The epilogue showed what happened to the characters after the story ended.
words.ex_cn: 尾声展示了故事结束后角色们的命运。
words.en: An epilogue is a section or speech at the end of a book or play that serves as a comment on or a conclusion to what has happened.

words.tr: n. 炉子；煤气头；燃烧器
words.ex: He turned on the burner to boil water.
words.ex_cn: 他打开炉子来烧水。
words.en: A burner is a device on a stove, cooker, or heater that produces a flame or heat for cooking or heating.

words.tr: n. 不重要的情况; v. 暂时搁置
words.ex: The project was put on the back-burner due to budget constraints.
words.ex_cn: 由于预算限制，该项目被暂时搁置。
words.en: A situation or project that is not being given immediate attention or priority.

words.ex: He arrived at the meeting pronto.
words.ex_cn: 他很快地赶到了会议。
words.en: Quickly; without delay.

words.ex: The river flows through a deep canyon.
words.ex_cn: 河流流经一个深峡谷。
words.en: A canyon is a large valley with very steep sides and usually a river flowing along the bottom.

words.tr: phrase. 本票；期票；一种书面承诺，由出票人签署，保证在指定日期或见票时无条件支付确定金额给持票人或指定人
words.ex: The bank issued a promissory note to secure the loan.
words.ex_cn: 银行发行了一张本票以确保贷款。
words.en: A promissory note is a financial instrument in which one party promises in writing to pay a determinate sum of money to the other, either at a fixed or determinable future time or on demand of the payee, under specific terms.

words.tr: adv. 按时间的前后顺序排列地
words.ex: He listed the events chronologically.
words.ex_cn: 他按时间顺序列出了这些事件。
words.en: In a manner that follows the order in which events occurred.

words.ex: He invests money in stocks.
words.ex_cn: 他投资股票。
words.en: If you invest in something, or if you invest a sum of money, you use your money in a way that you hope will increase its value, for example by putting it in a bank, or buying shares or property.

words.ex: He wisely saved money for the future.
words.ex_cn: 他明智地为将来存钱。
words.en: In a way that shows good judgment or the benefit of experience.

words.tr:
n. 后部；
v. 饲养；抚养；
adj. 后面的；
words.ex: The rear of the car was damaged in the accident.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的后部在事故中受损了。
words.en: The back part of something, especially a building or vehicle; to bring up and care for a child until they are fully grown.

words.ex: Check the rear-view mirror before changing lanes.
words.ex_cn: 变道前检查后视镜。
words.en: A rear-view mirror is a mirror in a vehicle that allows the driver to see the area behind the vehicle.

words.ex: We had dinner at a buffet with many dishes to choose from.
words.ex_cn: 我们在自助餐吃了晚饭，有很多菜可以选。
words.en: A buffet is a meal consisting of several dishes from which guests serve themselves. As a verb, to buffet means to strike repeatedly and violently.

words.ex: He crammed the suitcase with clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他把衣服塞满了行李箱。
words.en: If you cram things or people into a place, you put them into it even though there is hardly enough room for them.

words.ex: The problem was solved ingeniously.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题被巧妙地解决了。
words.en: In a manner showing cleverness or originality in solving problems or in inventing.

words.tr: adj. 有独创性的；巧妙的；
words.ex: The child came up with an ingenious way to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子想出了一个有独创性的方式来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Something that is ingenious is very clever and involves new ideas, methods, or equipment.

words.ex: He eats a cucumber for lunch.
words.ex_cn: 他午餐吃了一根黄瓜。
words.en: A cucumber is a long, green vegetable with a high water content, used in salads and for pickling.

words.ex: He skipped the hard question and moved to the next one.
words.ex_cn: 他略过了难题，继续做下一题。
words.en: To move lightly and quickly, making a small jump after each step.

words.tr: phrase. 叉车；铲车（一种用于搬运和堆垛托盘货物的工业车辆）
words.ex: The worker drives a forklift truck to move boxes.
words.ex_cn: 工人开叉车搬运箱子。
words.en: A forklift truck is a vehicle with a pronged device in front for lifting and carrying heavy loads.

words.tr: adj. <英><俚>筋疲力尽的 v. 杀死，使筋疲力尽( knacker的过去式和过去分词 )
words.ex: After the long hike, I was completely knackered.
words.ex_cn: 长途徒步之后，我完全筋疲力尽了。
words.en: If you say that you are knackered, you are emphasizing that you are extremely tired.

words.tr: n. 平底雪橇（toboggan 的变形）
words.ex: The tobogganist skillfully navigated the snowy slope.
words.ex_cn: 这位平底雪橇滑雪者熟练地滑下雪坡。
words.en: A person who rides a toboggan, especially as a sport or for recreation.

words.ex: He is patently lying about his age.
words.ex_cn: 他明显在谎报自己的年龄。
words.en: In a way that is clear and obvious to anyone.

words.ex: He got a patent for his new invention.
words.ex_cn: 他为自己的新发明获得了专利。
words.en: A patent is an official right to be the only person or company allowed to make or sell a new product for a certain period of time.

words.ex: The painting gave me inspiration.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画给了我灵感。
words.en: Inspiration is a feeling of enthusiasm you get from someone or something, which gives you new and creative ideas.

words.tr: adj. 分子的；分子构成的；
words.ex: Water is a molecular compound.
words.ex_cn: 水是一种分子化合物。
words.en: Relating to or consisting of molecules.

words.ex: Water is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom in a molecule.
words.ex_cn: 水由两个氢原子和一个氧原子组成一个分子。
words.en: A molecule is the smallest particle in a chemical element or compound that has the chemical properties of that element or compound. Molecules are made up of atoms that are held together by chemical bonds.

words.ex: The teacher will allot five minutes for questions.
words.ex_cn: 老师会分配五分钟提问。
words.en: If something is allotted to someone, it is given to them as their share.

words.ex: The book has a finite number of pages.
words.ex_cn: 这本书的页数是有限的。
words.en: Something that is finite has a definite fixed size or extent.

words.ex: He permanently moved to Canada last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年永久搬到了加拿大。
words.en: In a way that continues or lasts forever without changing.

words.ex: He used a spanner to tighten the bolts on the machine.
words.ex_cn: 他用扳手拧紧机器上的螺栓。
words.en: A spanner is a tool used for gripping and turning nuts or bolts.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必定的；
words.ex: It is inevitable that the sun will rise tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 太阳明天一定会升起。
words.en: If something is inevitable, it is certain to happen and cannot be prevented or avoided.

words.ex: He believed that providence would protect him.
words.ex_cn: 他相信上帝会保护他。
words.en: Providence refers to the protective care of God or of nature as a spiritual power, or the timely preparation for future eventualities.

words.ex: He stopped halfway to rest.
words.ex_cn: 他在半路停下来休息。
words.en: At or to a point midway between two others.

words.tr: n. 收割者；收获者；收割机
words.ex: The reaper cuts wheat in the field.
words.ex_cn: 收割者在田里收割小麦。
words.en: A reaper is a person or machine that cuts and gathers crops at harvest.

words.tr: phrase. 死神（常指手持镰刀收割生命的象征形象）
words.ex: The Reaper comes for everyone eventually.
words.ex_cn: 死神终将降临到每个人身上。
words.en: The reaper refers to someone or something that reaps, especially a person who cuts down crops at harvest time, or a figure representing death, who is often depicted as carrying a scythe.

words.tr: phrase. 死神（西方文化中象征死亡的拟人化形象，通常被描绘为披着黑斗篷、手持大镰刀的骷髅）
words.ex: The Grim Reaper symbolizes the inevitability of death.
words.ex_cn: 死神象征着死亡的不可避免。
words.en: The Grim Reaper is a personification of death, often depicted as a skeletal figure cloaked in black, wielding a scythe. This figure is used in various cultures to represent the inevitability of death.

words.tr:
v. 逝去；过去
n. （光阴）逝去
words.ex: Two hours elapsed while he waited for the bus.
words.ex_cn: 他等公交车时，两个小时过去了。
words.en: If time elapses, it passes.

words.tr: n. 乌贼; 乌贼属; 乌贼的墨; 颜料 adj. 乌贼墨色的，使用乌贼墨颜料的
words.ex: The artist used sepia tones to give the painting an antique feel.
words.ex_cn: 艺术家使用乌贼墨色调给画作增添了一种古旧的感觉。
words.en: A dark brown pigment or ink prepared from the secretion of the cuttlefish, used in drawing and in monochrome photography; a dark reddish-brown color.

words.ex: He read a biography of Nelson Mandela.
words.ex_cn: 他读了一本关于纳尔逊·曼德拉的传记。
words.en: A biography is a detailed description of a person's life. It involves more than just the basic facts like education, work, relationships, and death; it portrays a person's experience of these life events.

words.ex: He made an omelette for breakfast.
words.ex_cn: 他为早餐做了一个煎蛋卷。
words.en: An omelette is a dish made by beating eggs and cooking them in a frying pan, often with other ingredients such as cheese, vegetables, or meat.

words.ex: The epitaph on his grave says, 'Beloved father and friend.'
words.ex_cn: 他墓碑上的墓志铭写着：‘受人爱戴的父亲和朋友。’
words.en: An epitaph is a short piece of writing or a poem about a dead person, especially one written on their gravestone.

chapters.name: We are all dying Phrases and expressions

words.tr: phrase. v. 查看某物；检查某物；试用某物
words.ex: Let me check something out on the internet.
words.ex_cn: 让我在网上查点东西。
words.en: To examine, inspect, or look at something; or to leave a hotel after paying the bill.

words.tr: phrase. 打字输入；键入（文字或数据）
words.ex: You need to type in your password to access the system.
words.ex_cn: 你需要输入密码才能访问系统。
words.en: To enter data or text into a computer or other electronic device by typing.

words.tr: phrase. 由某人决定；取决于某人；责任在某人
words.ex: It's down to you to decide what to do next.
words.ex_cn: 下一步该怎么做由你来决定。
words.en: If something is down to a particular person, they are responsible for it or have the right to make decisions about it.

words.tr: 短语. ……的核心部分；……的实质内容（常用于比喻，指某事物最重要的部分）
words.ex: This is the meat of the problem we need to solve.
words.ex_cn: 这就是我们需要解决的问题的核心。
words.en: the essential or most important part of something

words.tr: phrase. 搁置的；暂缓的；处于次要地位的
words.ex: The project has been put on the back burner until we get more resources.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目在我们获得更多资源之前一直被搁置。
words.en: If something is on the back burner, it is temporarily not being dealt with or considered, especially because other things are more important.

words.w: be in a position to do
words.tr: 短语动词. 有能力做某事；处于能做某事的地位或状况
words.uk: biː ɪn ə pəˈzɪʃən tuː duː
words.us: biː ɪn ə pəˈzɪʃn tə duː
words.ex: She will be in a position to help you after she finishes her work.
words.ex_cn: 她完成工作后就能帮你了。
words.en: If you are in a position to do something, you are able to do it because you have the necessary ability, money, or power.

words.w: be in no position to do
words.tr: phrase. 处于无能力或无资格做某事的状态；没有条件或立场去做某事
words.ex: He was in no position to negotiate after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 失去工作后，他没有能力去谈判。
words.en: If you say that someone is in no position to do something, you mean that they are unable to do it, usually because they do not have the authority, knowledge, or ability to do so.

words.tr: 短语动词. 尝试做某事；争取某事的机会
words.ex: Why don't you have a shot at solving the problem?
words.ex_cn: 你为什么不试试解决这个问题呢？
words.en: To attempt to do something, especially something that is challenging or that you have not done before.

words.w: have a shot at doing sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 尝试做某事；争取做某事的机会
words.uk: hæv ə ʃɒt æt ˈduːɪŋ sʌmθɪŋ
words.us: hæv ə ʃɑːt æt ˈduːɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: Why don't you have a shot at doing it yourself?
words.ex_cn: 为什么不你自己试试看呢？
words.en: To attempt to do something, especially when it is challenging or you are not sure if you will succeed.

words.tr: 短语动词. 有机会尝试某事；获得做某事的机会
words.ex: I hope to get a shot at the new project.
words.ex_cn: 我希望有机会参与这个新项目。
words.en: To have an opportunity to try something or to do something.

words.w: get a shot at doing sth.
words.tr: 短语动词. 有机会尝试做某事
words.uk: ɡet ə ʃɒt æt ˈduːɪŋ sʌmθɪŋ
words.us: ɡet ə ʃɑːt æt ˈduːɪŋ ˈsʌmθɪŋ
words.ex: He finally got a shot at doing the job he always wanted.
words.ex_cn: 他终于有机会做他一直想做的工作了。
words.en: To have an opportunity to try doing something.

words.tr: phrase. 充分利用某事；尽力把不利情况变为有利；善处逆境
words.ex: She decided to make the best of the situation and enjoy the trip despite the bad weather.
words.ex_cn: 她决定尽量利用这个情况，尽管天气不好，还是享受这次旅行。
words.en: To use or deal with something in a way that achieves as much as possible, especially in a difficult situation.

words.tr: phrase. 放某人鸽子；约定见面却故意不到场
words.ex: She stood her date up last night.
words.ex_cn: 她昨晚放了她约会的鸽子。
words.en: To fail to meet someone for a date or appointment without informing them in advance.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人妥协；对某人作出让步；迁就对方
words.ex: She decided to meet him halfway and agreed to his proposal.
words.ex_cn: 她决定迁就他，同意了他的提议。
words.en: To compromise or make a concession to someone in order to reach an agreement.

chapters.name: Rites of passage New words

words.ex: He writes a letter every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天写一封信。
words.en: To write means to form letters, words, or symbols on a surface in order to communicate.

words.tr: phrase. 人生过渡仪式；通过仪式；标志着从一种社会地位或阶段过渡到另一种的典礼
words.ex: Graduation is considered a rite of passage for many students.
words.ex_cn: 毕业被许多学生视为一种通过仪式。
words.en: A rite of passage is a ceremony or event that marks an important stage in someone's life, especially the transition from childhood to adulthood.

words.ex: He had a fatalistic attitude towards his career.
words.ex_cn: 他对职业生涯持宿命论的态度。
words.en: A fatalistic person believes that all events are predetermined and therefore inevitable.

words.ex: The big rock was an obstacle on the road.
words.ex_cn: 那块大石头是路上的障碍。
words.en: An obstacle is something which makes it difficult for you to go forward or to achieve something.

words.ex: The obstacle race included hurdles, walls, and water obstacles.
words.ex_cn: 障碍赛包括跨栏、墙壁和水障碍。
words.en: An obstacle race is a race in which runners have to jump over, crawl under, or otherwise negotiate various obstacles.

words.ex: The contestant won the singing competition.
words.ex_cn: 这位竞争者赢得了歌唱比赛。
words.en: A contestant is someone who takes part in a competition or contest.

words.tr: adj. 至关重要的；决定性的；
words.ex: It is crucial to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水至关重要。
words.en: If you describe something as crucial, you mean it is extremely important.

words.ex: The clown made the children laugh.
words.ex_cn: 小丑让孩子们笑了。
words.en: A clown is a performer, typically in a circus, who wears a traditional costume and exaggerated makeup, and entertains by performing comedic acts.

words.ex: He wore a formal suit to the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他穿了一套正式的西装去参加婚礼。
words.en: Something that is formal is done or said according to an established or conventional way, especially in an official or serious situation.

words.ex: The government imposed a new tax on sugar.
words.ex_cn: 政府对糖征收了一项新税。
words.en: To impose means to officially force a rule, tax, punishment, etc. to be obeyed or received.

words.ex: This rule is universally accepted.
words.ex_cn: 这条规则被普遍接受。
words.en: In a way that is done or shared by all people or things in the world or in a particular group.

words.ex: The transition from school to work was hard for him.
words.ex_cn: 从学校到工作的转变对他来说很难。
words.en: The process or a period of changing from one state or condition to another.

words.ex: He reached adulthood at age 18.
words.ex_cn: 他在18岁时成年。
words.en: The period of time in a person's life when they are fully developed physically and mentally.

words.ex: They had a feast on New Year's Day.
words.ex_cn: 他们在元旦举办了一场盛宴。
words.en: A feast is a large and special meal, often to celebrate something.

words.tr: phrase. （犹太教中男孩子的）成年礼，通常在13岁时举行
words.ex: He celebrated his bar mitzvah last year.
words.ex_cn: 他去年庆祝了他的受诫礼。
words.en: A bar mitzvah is a Jewish religious ceremony and celebration for a boy who has reached the age of 13, marking his transition to adulthood in the Jewish community.

words.ex: He works legally in this country.
words.ex_cn: 他在该国合法工作。
words.en: In a way that is allowed or required by law.

words.tr: n. 正式舞会，毕业舞会
words.ex: He wore a suit to the prom.
words.ex_cn: 他穿西装去参加毕业舞会。
words.en: A prom is a formal dance held for a high school or college class, typically at the end of the academic year.

words.ex: He rode in a limousine to the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 他坐豪华轿车去参加婚礼。
words.en: A limousine is a large, luxurious car, especially one driven by a chauffeur and having a partition separating the passengers from the driver.

words.tr: n. （名人或要人走进人群的）露面闲谈; 在内地的长途徒步旅行
words.ex: The politician's walkabout was a great success, engaging with many voters.
words.ex_cn: 这位政治家的街头露面非常成功，与许多选民进行了交流。
words.en: A walkabout is a journey on foot undertaken by an Australian Aboriginal in order to live in the traditional manner. It can also refer to a public stroll taken by an important person, especially a member of a royal family, to meet people informally.

words.tr:
n. 青少年；
adj. 青少年的；
words.ex: The adolescent walked to school with his friends.
words.ex_cn: 这个青少年和朋友们一起走路去上学。
words.en: An adolescent is a young person who is developing into an adult.

words.ex: Water can penetrate the soil slowly.
words.ex_cn: 水可以慢慢渗透进土壤。
words.en: To penetrate means to enter or pass through something, especially when this is difficult or when it is not obvious how to do it.

words.ex: The aboriginal people live in the forests of Australia.
words.ex_cn: 土著居民生活在澳大利亚的森林里。
words.en: An aboriginal person or thing is one that has been in a country or region from the earliest known times or from before the arrival of colonists.

words.ex: The rain was continuous all day.
words.ex_cn: 雨一整天都在下个不停。
words.en: Something that is continuous happens or exists without stopping or being interrupted.

chapters.name: The Glass Castle New words

words.ex: He deceived his friend with a lie.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个谎言欺骗了朋友。
words.en: If you deceive someone, you make them believe something that is not true, usually in order to get some advantage for yourself.

words.ex: The elf lives in a small tree house.
words.ex_cn: 精灵住在一间小树屋里。
words.en: In folklore, an elf is a type of supernatural being in Germanic mythology and folklore. Elves are often depicted as youthful-seeming men and women of great beauty living in forests and other natural places, underground, or in wells and springs.

words.tr:
n. 标签；
v. 用标签标明；
words.ex: The bottle has a label with the name of the drink.
words.ex_cn: 瓶子上有一个写着饮料名称的标签。
words.en: A label is a piece of paper, polymer, cloth, metal, or other material affixed to a container or article, on which is written or printed information or symbols about the product or item.

words.tr: v. 洗脑；通过宣传说服
words.ex: He was brainwashed by the cult.
words.ex_cn: 他被这个邪教洗脑了。
words.en: To brainwash someone means to make them believe something by continually telling them that it is true and preventing them from thinking about it properly.

words.ex: It's a myth that eating late at night causes weight gain.
words.ex_cn: 晚上吃东西会导致发胖，这是一种错误观念。
words.en: A myth is a traditional story, especially one concerning the early history of a people or explaining some natural or social phenomenon, and typically involving supernatural beings or events.

words.ex: He picked up some flowers from the roadside.
words.ex_cn: 他从路边摘了一些花。
words.en: The edge of a road, especially a country road, where people can park or walk.

words.tr: n. 金银丝织品，华而不实，金属箔 adj. 闪亮的，俗丽的，华而不实的 vt. 用金箔装饰
words.ex: The Christmas tree was adorned with tinsel and colorful ornaments.
words.ex_cn: 圣诞树上装饰着金银丝和彩色装饰品。
words.en: Tinsel is a decoration consisting of thin strips of shiny metal foil, traditionally used at Christmas.

words.ex: The statue is made of white marble.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像由白色大理石制成。
words.en: Marble is a type of very hard rock which is used for making statues and for building. It is usually white with dark lines in it.

words.ex: He used a slingshot to hunt small birds.
words.ex_cn: 他用弹弓打小鸟。
words.en: A slingshot is a Y-shaped stick or piece of metal with a piece of elastic attached to the two top ends, used for shooting small stones.

words.tr: n. 方式；道路；方向；路线；方法；
words.ex: He found a new way to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他找到了一种解决这个问题的新方式。
words.en: A way is a method, style, or manner of doing something, or a route or path that you take to get from one place to another.

words.ex: He uses gypsum to make plaster for walls.
words.ex_cn: 他用石膏来制作墙面的灰泥。
words.en: A soft white or gray mineral consisting of hydrated calcium sulfate, used in making plaster of Paris and in the building industry.

words.tr: n. 领班；工头；陪审团主席
words.ex: The foreman told the workers to start the job.
words.ex_cn: 工头告诉工人们开始工作。
words.en: A foreman is a skilled and experienced worker who is in charge of a group of workers, especially in a factory or on a building site.

words.tr: n. 一个特殊日子的前夕或前夜
words.ex: The eve of Christmas is very special.
words.ex_cn: 圣诞节前夜非常特别。
words.en: The period of time immediately before an event or occasion, especially the day before a holiday or festival.

words.tr: n. 星座；一群杰出人物；一系列（相关的想法、事物）
words.ex: He saw the Orion constellation in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 他在夜空中看到了猎户座。
words.en: A constellation is a group of stars which form a pattern and have a name.

words.tr: v. 导航；应付（复杂情况）；
words.ex: He uses a map to navigate the city.
words.ex_cn: 他用地图来导航这座城市。
words.en: To navigate is to plan and direct the route or course of a ship, aircraft, or other form of transport, especially by using instruments or maps.

words.tr: n. 意大利人，西班牙人
words.ex: He was often mocked for his dago accent.
words.ex_cn: 他经常因为他的意大利口音而被嘲笑。
words.en: A derogatory term for a person of Italian or Spanish descent.

words.ex: He uses logic to solve the puzzle.
words.ex_cn: 他用逻辑来解决这个谜题。
words.en: Logic is a method of reasoning that involves a series of statements, each of which must be true if the statement before it is true.

words.tr:
v. 闪耀；闪烁
n. 闪烁
words.ex: The stars twinkle in the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星在夜空中闪烁。
words.en: If a star or a light twinkles, it shines with an unsteady light that rapidly and gently changes from bright to faint.

words.ex: The cake has three layers of chocolate.
words.ex_cn: 这个蛋糕有三层巧克力。
words.en: A layer of a substance or material is a quantity or piece of it that covers a surface or that is between two other things.

words.tr: adj. <俚>极小的，不足道的，整洁的
words.ex: She lived in a dinky little house by the river.
words.ex_cn: 她住在河边一间极小的房子里。
words.en: If you describe something as dinky, you mean that it is very small and neat, but often also that it is rather old-fashioned.

words.tr: n. 地平线；思想等的范围；眼界；
words.ex: The sun set below the horizon.
words.ex_cn: 太阳在地平线以下落山。
words.en: The horizon is the line at which the earth's surface and the sky appear to meet.

words.tr: phrase. 光年（天文学中使用的距离单位，指光在一年中行进的距离）
words.ex: The star is many light years away from Earth.
words.ex_cn: 这颗星星离地球有好多光年远。
words.en: A unit of astronomical distance equivalent to the distance that light travels in one year, which is 9.4607 × 10^12 km (nearly 6 trillion miles).

words.ex: The star fell into a black hole.
words.ex_cn: 这颗恒星落入了一个黑洞。
words.en: A black hole is a region of space having a gravitational field so intense that no matter or radiation can escape.

words.ex: The quasar is very far away and very bright.
words.ex_cn: 这个类星体非常遥远且非常明亮。
words.en: A quasar is a massive and extremely remote celestial object, emitting exceptionally large amounts of energy, and typically having a star-like image in a telescope.

words.ex: The star exploded into a supernova.
words.ex_cn: 那颗恒星爆炸成了超新星。
words.en: A supernova is the explosion of a star, which causes it to become extremely bright and then fade away over several weeks or months.

words.tr: n. 年久失修的旧机器; 破旧不堪的汽车 ; 严重的错误; 大错
words.ex: The car is a real clunker, it breaks down every other day.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车真是破旧不堪，每隔一天就出故障。
words.en: A clunker is an old car that is in very bad condition.

words.ex: The runner won the race quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这位跑步者很快赢得了比赛。
words.en: A runner is a person who runs, especially in a race or as a sport.

words.ex: The magnet has a magnetic force.
words.ex_cn: 这块磁铁有磁性。
words.en: If you describe something as magnetic, you mean that it is very attractive to people because it has unusual, powerful, and exciting qualities.

words.ex: He is a descendant of the first king.
words.ex_cn: 他是第一位国王的后裔。
words.en: A person, plant, or animal that is descended from a particular ancestor.

words.tr: n. 废旧杂物；无价值的东西；
words.ex: He cleaned up the junk in his garage.
words.ex_cn: 他清理了车库里那些废旧杂物。
words.en: Old or discarded articles that are considered useless or of little value.

chapters.name: The Glass Castle Phrases and expressions

words.tr: phrase. 轻视某人；看不起某人
words.ex: She always looks down on people who are less successful than her.
words.ex_cn: 她总是瞧不起那些不如她成功的人。
words.en: To regard someone as inferior or unworthy of respect.

words.tr: phrase. 轻视某事；看不起某事；对某事持蔑视态度
words.ex: She tends to look down on people who don't have a college education.
words.ex_cn: 她往往看不起没有大学学历的人。
words.en: If you look down on someone or something, you consider them to be inferior or unimportant in comparison to yourself or to something else.

words.tr: n. 标低价，[物价] 减价
words.ex: The store gave a markdown on all summer clothes.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有夏季服装进行了减价。
words.en: A reduction in the price of something, especially in a retail context.

words.tr: phrase. 失去理智的；发疯的；精神错乱的
words.ex: She must be out of her mind to think that would work.
words.ex_cn: 她一定是神智不清才会认为那会起作用。
words.en: To be unable to think or behave in a reasonable way because of extreme emotion or mental illness.

words.tr: phrase. 发疯；失去理智；精神失常
words.ex: He will go out of his mind if he hears the bad news.
words.ex_cn: 如果他听到那个坏消息，他会发疯的。
words.en: To become insane or to lose one's ability to think clearly.

words.tr: phrase. 永久地；长久地；一劳永逸地
words.ex: He decided to stay in the city for keeps.
words.ex_cn: 他决定永远留在城里。
words.en: Permanently; forever.

words.tr: phrase. 完全一样地；丝毫不差地（用于强调程度相当）
words.ex: She is every bit as talented as her sister.
words.ex_cn: 她和她的姐姐一样有才华。
words.en: used to emphasize that someone or something is just as good, important, etc. as someone or something else

words.tr: phrase. 声称对某物拥有权利；宣称对某事物有所有权
words.ex: He laid claim to the inheritance after his father's death.
words.ex_cn: 父亲去世后，他对遗产提出了所有权要求。
words.en: To assert one's right to something; to state that one has a right to something.

words.tr: phrase. （表示愤怒、惊讶或困惑）到底，究竟（用于加强语气）
words.ex: What the hell is going on?
words.ex_cn: 到底发生什么事了？
words.en: used to express frustration, surprise, or emphasis (often informal)

chapters.name: Cultural childhoods New words

words.ex: The transformation of the old factory into a park made the city nicer.
words.ex_cn: 把旧工厂改造成公园让城市变得更美了。
words.en: A transformation is a complete change in the appearance, form, or nature of something or someone.

words.ex: The consumption of water has increased this year.
words.ex_cn: 今年水的消耗量增加了。
words.en: Consumption is the act of buying and using products.

words.ex: The teacher said the answer is acceptable.
words.ex_cn: 老师说这个答案是可以接受的。
words.en: Something that is acceptable is satisfactory or good enough to be allowed or approved of.

words.ex: The teacher made an intervention to help the student.
words.ex_cn: 老师进行了干预以帮助学生。
words.en: Intervention is the act of intervening, especially in a situation to prevent something undesirable from happening.

words.ex: The prosecution brought evidence against the suspect.
words.ex_cn: 起诉方提供了针对嫌疑人的证据。
words.en: The act or process of holding a trial against a person who is accused of a crime to see if they are guilty.

words.ex: The old house has a colonial style.
words.ex_cn: 这所老房子具有殖民地风格。
words.en: Colonial means relating to a system or period of colonization, or to the people who live in a colony.

words.ex: She knit a warm scarf for her brother.
words.ex_cn: 她为她的弟弟织了一条暖和的围巾。
words.en: If you knit something, especially an article of clothing, you make it from wool or a similar thread by using two knitting needles or a machine.

words.ex: He wears a mitten to keep his hand warm.
words.ex_cn: 他戴一只连指手套来暖手。
words.en: A mitten is a glove that has one section for the thumb and another section for all four fingers together, used to keep the hands warm in cold weather.

words.ex: She made an embroidery of a flower on the pillow.
words.ex_cn: 她在枕头上绣了一朵花。
words.en: Embroidery is the craft of decorating fabric or other materials using a needle to apply thread or yarn. It may also incorporate other materials such as pearls, beads, quills, and sequins.

words.ex: He strictly follows the rules.
words.ex_cn: 他严格遵守规则。
words.en: In a manner that involves rigid enforcement or that demands complete conformity or exactness.

words.tr: n. 理解；了解； v. “understand”的现在分词；
words.ex: His understanding of the problem helped solve it quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题的理解帮助快速解决了它。
words.en: An understanding is a mutual agreement or sympathy between people or groups.

words.ex: The anthropologist studies ancient tribes.
words.ex_cn: 这位人类学家研究古代部落。
words.en: An anthropologist is a person who studies anthropology, which is the study of human societies and cultures and their development.

words.ex: He is largely responsible for the project's success.
words.ex_cn: 他主要对这个项目的成功负责。
words.en: To a great extent; mostly.

words.ex: He is incapable of solving simple math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他无法解决简单的数学问题。
words.en: If someone is incapable of doing something, they are unable to do it.

words.ex: The external wall of the house is painted blue.
words.ex_cn: 房子的外墙被刷成了蓝色。
words.en: External is used to indicate that something is on the outside of a surface or body, or that it exists, happens, or comes from outside.

words.ex: The judge showed leniency toward the first-time offender.
words.ex_cn: 法官对初犯表现出了宽大。
words.en: Leniency is the quality of being more merciful or tolerant than expected.

words.ex: His competence in math helped him solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他在数学方面的能力帮助他解决了这个问题。
words.en: Competence is the ability to do something well or efficiently.

words.tr: adj. 调皮的；恶作剧的；有害的
words.ex: The mischievous boy laughed and hid his sister's shoes.
words.ex_cn: 那个顽皮的男孩笑着藏起了他姐姐的鞋子。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as mischievous, you mean that they enjoy playing tricks on people or doing things to annoy or embarrass them.

words.tr: v. 击败；敲打；“beat”的现在分词； n. 打；打败；
words.ex: Our team was beating the rivals in the final match.
words.ex_cn: 我们的队伍在决赛中击败了对手。
words.en: The act of hitting someone or something repeatedly, or a defeat in a game or competition.

words.tr: adj. （指坏事）故意的; （指人）任性的，固执的
words.ex: He made a wilful mistake on purpose.
words.ex_cn: 他故意犯了一个顽固的错误。
words.en: If you describe actions or attitudes as wilful, you are critical of them because they are done or expressed deliberately, especially with the intention of causing harm, or they show a stubborn and determined desire to do what you want, regardless of what anyone else thinks.

words.ex: The desert has a harsh climate.
words.ex_cn: 沙漠的气候非常严酷。
words.en: If you describe something as harsh, you mean that it is extremely difficult and unpleasant to live in, do, or experience, especially because it is very cold, hot, or violent.

words.tr: n. 局外人；无取胜希望者；
words.ex: He felt like an outsider at the party.
words.ex_cn: 他在聚会上感觉像个局外人。
words.en: An outsider is someone who does not belong to a particular group or organization.

words.ex: He radically changed his mind about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他彻底改变了对这个计划的想法。
words.en: In a way that is very different from the usual or traditional way.

words.ex: The festival celebrates ethnic music and dance.
words.ex_cn: 这个节日庆祝民族音乐和舞蹈。
words.en: Ethnic relates to a group of people who have a common national or cultural tradition.

words.ex: She has traveled extensively across Europe.
words.ex_cn: 她广泛地游历了欧洲。
words.en: Something that is extensive covers a wide range of details, ideas, or items.

words.ex: He was reluctant to leave his home.
words.ex_cn: 他不愿意离开家。
words.en: If you are reluctant to do something, you are unwilling to do it and hesitate before doing it, or do it slowly and without enthusiasm.

words.tr: adj. 极饥饿的； v. “famish”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He was famished after running for five hours.
words.ex_cn: 他跑了五个小时后饿极了。
words.en: If you are famished, you are extremely hungry.

words.tr:
n. 接触；联系；
v. 接触；联系；
words.ex: The two balls made contact when they collided.
words.ex_cn: 两个球在碰撞时发生了接触。
words.en: Contact refers to the act of communicating with someone, especially regularly, or the state of touching something.

words.ex: He showed reverence for his grandfather.
words.ex_cn: 他对祖父表示尊敬。
words.en: A feeling of profound respect for someone or something.

words.tr: adj. 无能力的；不称职的；不能胜任的；
words.ex: He is incompetent at managing simple tasks.
words.ex_cn: 他无法胜任简单的任务。
words.en: If you describe someone as incompetent, you are criticizing them because they are unable to do their job or a task properly.

words.tr:
adj. 依靠的；依赖的；
n. 受赡养者；
words.ex: The child is dependent on his parents for food.
words.ex_cn: 这个孩子依靠父母提供食物。
words.en: A dependent person or thing is one that needs the support of another person or thing in order to exist or be successful.

words.tr: n. 儿童托管；儿童保育；
words.ex: She works in childcare for young children.
words.ex_cn: 她从事幼儿托管工作。
words.en: The care of children, especially by a service or organization.

words.tr: adj. 无人监督的；无人管理的；
words.ex: The children played in the park in an unsupervised way.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在无人监督的情况下在公园里玩耍。
words.en: Not watched or managed by someone in authority.

words.tr: adj. 不负责任的；无责任感的；
words.ex: He is irresponsible because he never pays his bills.
words.ex_cn: 他从不付账单，所以是不负责任的。
words.en: If you describe someone as irresponsible, you are criticizing them because they do things without properly considering their possible consequences.

words.ex: He collected firewood for the campfire.
words.ex_cn: 他为篝火收集了木柴。
words.en: Wood that is cut and used for fuel in fires.

words.ex: He has a clear notion of right and wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他对对错有清晰的概念。
words.en: A notion is an idea or belief about something.

words.ex: He is a teen who loves basketball.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个喜欢篮球的十几岁少年。
words.en: A teen is a young person whose age is between thirteen and nineteen.

words.ex: The government imposed a new tax on sugar.
words.ex_cn: 政府对糖征收了一项新税。
words.en: To impose means to officially force a rule, tax, punishment, etc. to be obeyed or received.

words.ex: His judgment was clear and fair.
words.ex_cn: 他的判断清晰而公正。
words.en: A judgment is an opinion that you have or express after thinking carefully about something.

words.tr: adj. 离奇的；奇特的；奇怪的；
words.ex: The clown wore a bizarre hat with three eyes.
words.ex_cn: 小丑戴着一顶有三只眼睛的离奇帽子。
words.en: Something that is bizarre is very odd and strange.

words.ex: He responded negatively to the proposal.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个提议持消极态度。
words.en: In a manner that is negative or pessimistic.

words.ex: The continual rain made the road very muddy.
words.ex_cn: 不停的雨让道路变得非常泥泞。
words.en: Something that is continual happens repeatedly over a period of time.

words.ex: The magic show had a strange fascination for children.
words.ex_cn: 魔术表演对孩子们有一种奇特的迷惑力。
words.en: A fascination is a very strong interest or attraction for someone or something.

words.tr: n. 视角；观点；（对事物的）合理判断；
words.ex: His perspective on life is very positive.
words.ex_cn: 他对生活的看法非常积极。
words.en: A particular attitude towards or way of regarding something; a point of view.

chapters.name: Cultural childhoods Phrases and expressions

words.tr: phrase. 为感谢…；为表彰…；出于对…的赞赏
words.ex: He received a gift in appreciation of his hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他收到了一份礼物，以感谢他的辛勤工作。
words.en: used to express gratitude or thanks for something someone has done

words.tr: phrase. 与…讲道理；劝说；以理说服
words.ex: He tried to reason with his little brother.
words.ex_cn: 他试图跟弟弟讲道理。
words.en: To try to persuade someone to act in a sensible way or to accept your explanation of something by talking to them in a logical manner.

words.tr: phrase. 训斥某人；责备某人
words.ex: The teacher told him off for being late.
words.ex_cn: 老师因为他迟到而责备了他。
words.en: To reprimand or scold someone.

words.tr: phrasal verb. 跌倒；被绊倒；翻倒
words.ex: The boy falls over and cries.
words.ex_cn: 男孩摔倒了，哭了。
words.en: To fall over means to fall to the ground or to fall down from an upright position.

words.tr: phrase. 对……表示反对；对……反感；对……提出异议
words.ex: He takes exception to people who are late.
words.ex_cn: 他看不惯迟到的人。
words.en: To object strongly to something; to be offended by something.

words.ex: He tends to arrive late for class.
words.ex_cn: 他总是迟到上课。
words.en: If someone or something tends to do a particular thing, they usually do it or they often do it.

chapters.name: Childhood around the world New words

words.ex: The view from the hill is marvellous.
words.ex_cn: 从山上看到的景色绝妙极了。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as marvellous, you are emphasizing that they are extremely good, enjoyable, or impressive.

words.ex: The king ate a sumptuous meal in his palace.
words.ex_cn: 国王在他的宫殿里享用了一顿丰盛的饭菜。
words.en: Something that is sumptuous is very impressive and expensive, especially in a way that involves large amounts of money.

words.tr: n. 食品贮藏室；食品柜
words.ex: She stored bread in the larder.
words.ex_cn: 她把面包存放在食品储藏室里。
words.en: A larder is a cool area in a house where food is stored.

words.ex: He is my fella from childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他是我从小的伙伴。
words.en: A fella is a man or boy, especially one who is considered to be ordinary or typical.

words.ex: The buyer paid for the car last week.
words.ex_cn: 买方上周支付了车款。
words.en: A buyer is a person who buys something, especially from a shop or another person.

words.ex: The robber stole a wallet from the man.
words.ex_cn: 劫匪从那个人那里偷了一个钱包。
words.en: A robber is a person who steals from another person or place, especially by using force or threats.

words.ex: He plays violin in a local orchestra.
words.ex_cn: 他在一个本地管弦乐队中拉小提琴。
words.en: An orchestra is a large group of musicians who play a variety of different instruments together. Orchestras usually play classical music.

chapters.name: How we listen New words

words.ex: He has the capacity to solve hard math problems.
words.ex_cn: 他有能力解决复杂的数学问题。
words.en: The capacity of a place or container is the amount of things or people that it can hold.

words.ex: He did it for her sake.
words.ex_cn: 他为了她的缘故做了这件事。
words.en: If you do something for the sake of something, you do it for that purpose or in order to achieve that result. You can also say that you do it for something's sake.

words.ex: The doctor used medical terminology to explain the illness.
words.ex_cn: 医生使用医学术语来解释这种疾病。
words.en: The set of terms and expressions used in a particular subject, field, or profession.

words.tr: adj. 感觉上的；感官的；（引起）美感的
words.ex: She wore a sensuous silk dress.
words.ex_cn: 她穿了一件性感的丝绸裙子。
words.en: Relating to or affecting the senses rather than the intellect; characterized by a pleasing or luxurious quality that appeals to the senses.

words.ex: Her expressive eyes showed all her feelings.
words.ex_cn: 她富有表情的眼睛展现了她所有的感情。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behaviour as expressive, you mean that their behaviour clearly indicates their feelings or intentions.

words.ex: She sheerly wants to be happy.
words.ex_cn: 她仅仅想快乐。
words.en: Completely; purely.

words.ex: He mechanically pressed the buttons without thinking.
words.ex_cn: 他机械地按下了按钮，没有思考。
words.en: In a manner that relates to or is operated by a machine or machinery; in a way that lacks thought or spontaneity.

words.ex: It is a hypothetical situation.
words.ex_cn: 这是一个假设的情况。
words.en: A hypothetical situation, idea, or explanation is based on possible ideas or situations rather than actual ones.

words.tr: adv. 心不在焉地；茫然地
words.ex: He absent-mindedly left his keys on the table.
words.ex_cn: 他心不在焉地把钥匙留在了桌上。
words.en: If someone does something absent-mindedly, they do it without thinking about it or without concentrating on it because they are thinking about something else.

words.ex: He gave a brainless answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了一个愚蠢的答案。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as brainless, you mean that they are stupid.

words.ex: Poverty can engender crime.
words.ex_cn: 贫困会引起犯罪。
words.en: To cause a feeling, situation, or condition to exist.

words.tr: adj. 有资格的；合格的； v. 取得资格；“qualify”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: He is a qualified teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有资格的老师。
words.en: Having the necessary qualifications for a particular job or task.

words.tr: v. 使合格；使具有资格；
words.ex: He studied hard to qualify for the job.
words.ex_cn: 他努力学习以获得这份工作的资格。
words.en: To qualify means to meet the necessary conditions or standards to be eligible for something or to perform a particular role.

words.ex: Her hug was a consolation after the loss.
words.ex_cn: 在失败之后，她的拥抱是一种安慰。
words.en: Consolation is something that makes you feel better when you are sad or disappointed.

words.tr:
adj. 恰当的；适宜的
adv. 恰当地；适宜地
prep. 关于；至于
words.ex: Your suggestion is apropos to our current needs.
words.ex_cn: 你的建议恰好符合我们当前的需求。
words.en: If something is apropos, it is suitable in a particular situation.

words.ex: The medicine is potent and works quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种药物非常有效，起效很快。
words.en: Something that is potent is very effective and powerful.

words.ex: He tried to usurp the throne from his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他试图从他兄弟手中篡夺王位。
words.en: If you say that someone usurps a job, role, title, or position, they take it from someone when they have no right to do this.

words.ex: The punishment was disproportionate to the crime.
words.ex_cn: 惩罚与罪行不成比例。
words.en: Something that is disproportionate is surprisingly large or small in comparison to something else.

words.ex: Five apples constitute a basket.
words.ex_cn: 五个苹果构成一篮子。
words.en: If something constitutes a particular thing, it can be regarded as being that thing.

words.ex: He is a composer who writes music for movies.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位为电影作曲的作曲家。
words.en: A composer is a person who writes music, especially classical music.

words.ex: The king proclaimed a new law.
words.ex_cn: 国王宣告了一项新法律。
words.en: If you proclaim something, you formally announce it or declare it publicly.

words.ex: He refused the money purely because it was wrong.
words.ex_cn: 他纯粹是因为觉得不对才拒绝了那笔钱。
words.en: In a pure manner; without admixture or adulteration.

words.tr: adj. 不妥协的；不让步的
words.ex: He is intransigent about his opinions.
words.ex_cn: 他对自己的观点毫不让步。
words.en: If you describe someone as intransigent, you mean that they refuse to behave differently or to change their attitude to something.

words.ex: The clock strikes precisely at noon.
words.ex_cn: 钟恰好在正午敲响。
words.en: In a precise manner; exactly.

words.tr: n. 赋格曲；朦胧状态；神游症
words.ex: He composed a fugue for the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他为钢琴创作了一首赋格曲。
words.en: A fugue is a piece of music that begins with a theme that is then repeated and developed by different voices or instruments in a structured manner.

words.tr:
n. 暴躁脾气；情绪；心情；性情
v. 使…缓和；冲淡
words.ex: He loses his temper when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 当他累了的时候，他会发脾气。
words.en: If you refer to someone's temper or say that they have a temper, you mean that they become angry very easily.

words.ex: He plays the clavichord in his quiet room.
words.ex_cn: 他在安静的房间里弹奏大键琴。
words.en: A clavichord is a European stringed keyboard instrument known from the late Medieval, through the Renaissance, Baroque and Classical eras.

words.ex: He felt sadness after losing his dog.
words.ex_cn: 他失去狗后感到悲伤。
words.en: Sadness is the feeling of being unhappy, especially because something bad has happened.

words.ex: He smiled pessimistically when he heard the news.
words.ex_cn: 当他听到这个消息时，他悲观地笑了笑。
words.en: In a manner that tends to see the worst aspect of things or believe that the worst will happen.

words.tr: adv. 顺从地; 听从地; 服从地
words.ex: He sighed resignedly when the boss said no.
words.ex_cn: 当老板说不行时，他无奈地叹了口气。
words.en: In a way that shows acceptance of something unpleasant or undesirable without resistance or complaint.

words.tr: adv. 致命地; 宿命地; 命中注定地; 与命运有关地
words.ex: He fatefully chose the wrong path.
words.ex_cn: 他命运般地选择了错误的路。
words.en: In a manner that is determined by fate or that has important consequences.

words.tr: adv. 笑眯眯; 微笑地; 带笑; 咪
words.ex: She waved at me smilingly.
words.ex_cn: 她微笑着向我挥手。
words.en: In a smiling manner; with a smile.

words.ex: This painting is a work of art.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画是一幅艺术品。
words.en: A work of art is something that is made with great skill, especially a painting, drawing, or sculpture.

words.tr: adj. 令人愉快的；愉悦的；
words.ex: The trip was a pleasurable experience.
words.ex_cn: 这次旅行是一次令人愉快的经历。
words.en: Something that is pleasurable is enjoyable or gives you pleasure.

words.ex: The politician used manipulation to win the election.
words.ex_cn: 这位政治家通过操纵赢得了选举。
words.en: Manipulation refers to the act of controlling or influencing someone or something in a skillful but often unfair or dishonest way.

words.ex: The water is sufficiently warm to swim.
words.ex_cn: 水温足够暖和，可以游泳。
words.en: To an adequate degree; enough.

words.ex: He was conscious after the accident.
words.ex_cn: 事故后他醒了过来。
words.en: If you are conscious of something, you notice it or are aware of it.

words.ex: He has awareness of the environmental problems.
words.ex_cn: 他意识到环境问题。
words.en: Knowledge or perception of a situation or fact.

words.ex: The baby smiled at the sweet melody.
words.ex_cn: 宝宝听到了甜美的旋律，笑了。
words.en: A melody is a sequence of single notes that is musically satisfying.

words.ex: The rhythm of the music made everyone dance.
words.ex_cn: 音乐的节奏让所有人都跳起了舞。
words.en: A rhythm is a regular series of sounds or movements.

words.ex: The clarity of her explanation helped everyone understand.
words.ex_cn: 她解释的清晰帮助了每个人理解。
words.en: Clarity is the quality of being clear, in particular the quality of being easy to understand or see.

words.ex: The data points correlate with each other.
words.ex_cn: 这些数据点相互关联。
words.en: If one thing correlates with another, there is a close similarity or connection between them, often because one thing causes the other.

words.ex: There is a correlation between exercise and good health.
words.ex_cn: 锻炼与健康之间存在相关性。
words.en: A correlation between things is a connection or link between them.

words.ex: The cat made an instinctive jump to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 猫本能地跳开以躲避狗。
words.en: An instinctive feeling, action, or idea is one that you have or do without thinking or reasoning.

words.ex: She instinctively reached for her phone when it rang.
words.ex_cn: 电话响时，她下意识地伸手去拿手机。
words.en: If you behave instinctively, you do something without thinking about it because it seems natural or the right thing to do.

words.ex: He used an analogy to explain how the heart works.
words.ex_cn: 他用了一个类比来解释心脏是如何工作的。
words.en: If you make or draw an analogy between two things, you show that they are similar in some way.

words.ex: The two situations are analogous.
words.ex_cn: 这两种情况是相似的。
words.en: If one thing is analogous to another, the two things are similar in some way.

words.ex: He wore a funny costume for the party.
words.ex_cn: 他为派对穿了一套滑稽的服装。
words.en: A costume is a set of clothes in a style typical of a particular country or historical period, or a set of clothes worn by an actor for a particular role.

words.ex: The theatrical lighting made the stage look magical.
words.ex_cn: 剧场的灯光让舞台显得神奇。
words.en: Theatrical means relating to the theatre or to the performance of plays. It can also describe behaviour that is exaggerated and intended to attract attention.

words.ex: We derive the answer from the formula.
words.ex_cn: 我们从公式中得到答案。
words.en: If you derive something such as pleasure or benefit from a person or from something, you get it from them.

words.ex: The children's laughter brought gaiety to the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们的笑声为派对带来了欢乐。
words.en: Gaiety is a feeling, attitude, or atmosphere of liveliness and fun.

words.tr:
n. 等价物；
adj. 相等的；等价的；
words.ex: The dollar is the equivalent of ten yuan.
words.ex_cn: 美元是十元的等价物。
words.en: If one amount or value is the equivalent of another, they are the same.

words.ex: He is a famous playwright who writes plays.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位著名的剧作家，写剧本。
words.en: A playwright is a person who writes plays.

words.ex: The theatergoer clapped loudly after the play.
words.ex_cn: 观剧者在演出结束后大声鼓掌。
words.en: A theatergoer is someone who regularly attends the theater to watch plays or performances.

words.ex: The children cleaned their rooms separately.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们分别打扫了自己的房间。
words.en: If people or things are dealt with separately, they are dealt with individually, not in a group.

chapters.name: How we listen Phrases and expressions

words.tr: phrase. 可以说；打个比方；在某种意义上
words.ex: He is a teacher, so to speak, helping students every day.
words.ex_cn: 他可以说是老师，每天都在帮助学生。
words.en: used to indicate that one is using a phrase or expression in an unusual or metaphorical way.

words.tr: phrase. 分手；分裂；解散；分摊
words.ex: They split up after the argument.
words.ex_cn: 他们在争吵后分开了。
words.en: To end a relationship or partnership; to divide or separate into parts.

words.tr: phrase. 回避；畏缩不前；不敢面对
words.ex: He shy away from speaking in front of people.
words.ex_cn: 他不敢在众人面前说话。
words.en: If you shy away from doing something, you avoid doing it, often because you are afraid or not confident enough.

words.ex: Heaven knows how much I tried.
words.ex_cn: 只有老天知道我有多努力。
words.en: Used to express that one does not know something and that it is impossible to find out.

words.tr: 短语. 使某人感到满意；令某人满意地
words.ex: He finished the work to his mother's satisfaction.
words.ex_cn: 他完成了工作，让母亲很满意。
words.en: In a way that pleases someone or meets their requirements.

words.tr: phrase. 把…固定住；找某人问清；确定
words.ex: He used a nail to pin down the map on the wall.
words.ex_cn: 他用钉子把地图固定在墙上。
words.en: To pin something down means to identify or define it clearly and precisely.

words.ex: The lamp gives off a warm light.
words.ex_cn: 这盏灯发出温暖的光。
words.en: If something gives off or gives out a gas, heat, or a smell, it produces it and sends it out into the air.

words.ex: This word derives from Latin.
words.ex_cn: 这个词源自拉丁语。
words.en: To obtain something from a specified source.

words.ex: Aside from John, everyone went to the party.
words.ex_cn: 不包括约翰，大家都去参加派对了。
words.en: You use aside from when you are making an exception to a general statement.

chapters.name: The photo New words

words.ex: He is practically always late for class.
words.ex_cn: 他几乎总是上课迟到。
words.en: In a way that is almost true or almost the case; virtually.

words.ex: He felt exhilaration after winning the race.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得比赛后感到兴奋不已。
words.en: Exhilaration is a feeling of being very happy and excited.

words.ex: The car exceeded the speed limit.
words.ex_cn: 这辆车超过了限速。
words.en: To be greater in quantity, degree, or intensity than something else.

words.tr: n. 用户；订户；捐献者；签署者
words.ex: He is a subscriber to the newspaper.
words.ex_cn: 他是这份报纸的订阅者。
words.en: A subscriber is a person who pays to receive a product or service regularly, such as a magazine or a service on the internet.

words.ex: He reads a science journal every week.
words.ex_cn: 他每周读一本科学期刊。
words.en: A journal is a newspaper or magazine that deals with a particular subject or professional activity.

words.ex: She wore a dress for the occasion.
words.ex_cn: 她为了这个特殊场合穿了一条裙子。
words.en: An occasion is a particular time when something happens, or a special event.

words.ex: His pursuit of happiness made him work hard every day.
words.ex_cn: 他对幸福的追求让他每天努力工作。
words.en: The act of pursuing something or someone, especially in order to catch or achieve them.

words.tr: adj. 突出的；杰出的；显著的；
words.ex: He is a prominent scientist in the field of medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他是医学领域的一位突出的科学家。
words.en: Someone or something that is prominent is important and well-known, or is positioned in a way that makes them easily seen or noticed.

words.ex: The photographer took pictures of the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 这位摄影家拍了日落的照片。
words.en: A photographer is a person who takes photographs, especially as a job.

words.ex: The clack of the typewriter filled the room.
words.ex_cn: 打字机的哒哒声充满了房间。
words.en: If things clack, they make a short loud noise, especially when they hit each other.

words.ex: The argument started small but soon escalate.
words.ex_cn: 争论起初很小，但很快逐步升高。
words.en: If a bad situation escalates or if someone or something escalates it, it becomes greater in size, seriousness, or intensity.

words.ex: The children caused a big commotion in the classroom.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在教室里制造了很大的喧闹。
words.en: A commotion is a lot of noise, confusion, and excitement.

words.ex: The store offers multiple flavors of ice cream.
words.ex_cn: 这家商店提供多种口味的冰淇淋。
words.en: If something is multiple, it consists of or involves many things of the same kind.

words.ex: The hawk made a sudden swoop to catch the mouse.
words.ex_cn: 老鹰突然俯冲下来抓老鼠。
words.en: To move very quickly and easily through the air, especially down from a height in order to attack.

words.tr:
v. 惊异于；惊异；
n. 令人惊异的人（或事）；
words.ex: I marvel at how fast she runs.
words.ex_cn: 我惊异于她跑得有多快。
words.en: If you marvel at something, you express your great surprise, wonder, or admiration.

words.tr:
v. 引起（问题、危险等）；提出；
n. 姿势；
words.ex: Pollution can pose a serious threat to health.
words.ex_cn: 污染可能对健康造成严重威胁。
words.en: If you pose for a photograph or painting, you stay in a particular position so that someone can photograph you or paint you. / To pose a question or problem means to ask it or to present it.

words.tr: n. 城河；壕坑; n. （Foss）人名；（德、英、法、西、瑞典）福斯
words.ex: The castle is surrounded by a deep foss.
words.ex_cn: 城堡被一条深城河环绕。
words.en: A fossilized remnant or trace of an organism from a past geological age.

words.ex: She bought a new perfume for the party.
words.ex_cn: 她为派对买了一瓶新香水。
words.en: A perfume is a pleasant-smelling liquid which people put on their skin to make themselves smell nice.

words.ex: He wears cologne every morning.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上都喷古龙水。
words.en: Cologne is a type of perfume that is not very strong and is often used by men.

words.tr: adj. 熙熙攘攘的； v. “bustle”的现在分词；
words.ex: The market is bustling with people.
words.ex_cn: 市场里人来人往，熙熙攘攘。
words.en: If a place is bustling, it is full of busy activity.

words.ex: The guitarist played a C major chord.
words.ex_cn: 吉他手弹了一个C大和弦。
words.en: A chord is a group of three or more musical notes played together.

words.ex: The onlooker watched the accident quietly.
words.ex_cn: 旁观者安静地看着这起事故。
words.en: A person who watches something happening without taking part in it.

words.ex: The viewer watched the movie on TV.
words.ex_cn: 观看者在电视上看了这部电影。
words.en: A viewer is someone who watches something, especially television.

words.tr:
n. 特征；报刊特写；
v. 以…为特色；是…的重要组成；
words.ex: The main feature of this phone is its long battery life.
words.ex_cn: 这款手机的主要特征是续航时间长。
words.en: A feature of something is an interesting or important part or characteristic of it.

words.tr:
v. 摇摆；摇动；
n. 影响；支配；
words.ex: The tree branches sway in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 树的枝条在风中摇摆。
words.en: To sway means to move slowly or rhythmically backwards and forwards or from side to side. It can also mean to influence someone or something.

words.ex: He fell and hurt his hip.
words.ex_cn: 他摔倒了，伤到了臀部。
words.en: The hip is the area on each side of the body below the waist and above the thigh.

words.ex: The statue has a strong torso.
words.ex_cn: 这座雕像有一个强壮的躯干。
words.en: The main part of the human body, not including the head, arms, or legs.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.tr:
adv. 向下地；
adj. 向下的；
words.ex: The leaves fell downward slowly.
words.ex_cn: 树叶慢慢向下飘落。
words.en: Moving or leading towards a lower place or level

words.tr: adv. 显然；表面上看起来；
words.ex: He is apparently late for the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他显然迟到了会议。
words.en: You use apparently to indicate that the information you are giving is something that you have heard, but you are not certain that it is true.

words.tr: adj. 没意识到的；不知道的；
words.ex: He was unaware of the rain until he got wet.
words.ex_cn: 他直到被淋湿了才意识到下雨了。
words.en: If you are unaware of something, you do not know about it.

words.tr: n. 追赶者；追寻者；追捕者
words.ex: The pursuer was relentless in his chase.
words.ex_cn: 追捕者对他的追逐毫不松懈。
words.en: A pursuer is someone who is following or chasing someone else, often in order to catch them.

words.tr: v. 漂白；“bleach”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The clothes were bleached in the sun.
words.ex_cn: 衣服在阳光下被漂白了。
words.en: If something is bleached, it has been made white or much lighter in color by a chemical process or by the sun.

words.ex: She added bleach to the white shirt to make it brighter.
words.ex_cn: 她往白衬衫里加了漂白剂，让它更亮。
words.en: To bleach something means to make it white or pale by using a chemical or by exposing it to sunlight.

words.tr: n. 司仪神父，天主教主领弥撒的神父
words.ex: The celebrant smiled at the crowd during the wedding.
words.ex_cn: 婚礼上，主持人对人群微笑。
words.en: A celebrant is a person who performs a rite, especially a priest at the Eucharist, or someone who is celebrating something.

words.ex: The law obliges parents to send their children to school.
words.ex_cn: 法律责成父母送孩子上学。
words.en: If you describe someone as obliging, you mean that they are willing and eager to be helpful.

words.ex: It was her maiden flight on a plane.
words.ex_cn: 这是她第一次坐飞机。
words.en: A maiden is a young girl or woman who is not married.

words.tr: adj. 随后的；后来的；接踵而至的； v. “ensue”的现在分词；
words.ex: The ensuing meeting was canceled.
words.ex_cn: 随后的会议被取消了。
words.en: Following immediately after something else.

words.ex: He used a match to ignite the fire.
words.ex_cn: 他用火柴点燃了火。
words.en: If you ignite something or if it ignites, it starts burning or explodes.

words.ex: He devised a new way to solve the problem.
words.ex_cn: 他设计了一种解决这个问题的新方法。
words.en: To devise something means to plan or invent a new way of doing something.

words.ex: The movie has a simple storyline.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影有一个简单的故事情节。
words.en: The plot or main story of a narrative, especially in a movie, novel, or play.

words.tr:
v. 补充；与…相辅相成；
n. 补足物；补语；余角；
words.ex: The red scarf complements her blue coat.
words.ex_cn: 这条红围巾补充了她的蓝外套。
words.en: To complement something means to make it complete or perfect by adding something to it.

words.tr:
v. 臆测；猜想
n. 臆测；猜度
words.ex: He surmises that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他推测明天会下雨。
words.en: If you surmise that something is true, you guess it from the available evidence, although you do not know for certain.

words.ex: The book has a gloss at the bottom of each page.
words.ex_cn: 这本书每页底部都有注释。
words.en: A gloss is a bright shine on the surface of something. It can also refer to a superficial appearance or interpretation that conceals the true nature of something.

words.tr: v. 使浪漫化；使传奇化；使夸张化
words.ex: She tends to romanticize the past.
words.ex_cn: 她倾向于将过去浪漫化。
words.en: To romanticize something means to make it seem more exciting or attractive than it really is.

words.tr: adv. 可预见地；可预言地
words.ex: He arrives late, predictably.
words.ex_cn: 他迟到了，这很可预见。
words.en: In a way that can be expected or foreseen.

words.ex: The weather was predictable today, just like yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 今天的天气和昨天一样，是可以预见的。
words.en: If you say that an event or a situation is predictable, you mean that it is obvious in advance that it will happen or what it will be like.

words.tr:
n. 高峰；顶峰；
v. 达到高峰；达到最高值；
words.ex: The mountain peak is covered with snow.
words.ex_cn: 这座山的高峰被雪覆盖。
words.en: The highest point or level of something; the pointed top of a mountain.

words.tr:
adj. 主要的；最重要的；
n. 校长；负责人；
words.ex: The principal reason for his success is hard work.
words.ex_cn: 他成功的主要原因是努力工作。
words.en: The person with the highest authority or most important position in an organization, institution, or group.

words.ex: The fish spawn in the river each spring.
words.ex_cn: 鱼每年春天在河里产卵。
words.en: To spawn means to produce or deposit eggs, especially in large quantities, as fish, frogs, etc. do. It can also mean to give rise to or generate something.

words.tr: n. 船的载货量，一条船的货物
words.ex: He brought a boatload of cookies to the party.
words.ex_cn: 他带了一大堆饼干去参加派对。
words.en: A boatload of something is a very large amount of it.

words.tr: adj. 感伤的；感情的；多愁善感的
words.ex: He kept the old toy because he was sentimental about it.
words.ex_cn: 他保留了那个旧玩具，因为他对它有感情。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as sentimental, you mean that they are influenced by emotional feelings, especially about happy memories of past events or relationships with other people, rather than by careful thought and judgment based on facts.

words.tr: n. 可能发生的情况；设想；
words.ex: It's a possible scenario that it will rain tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 明天会下雨是一个可能发生的情况。
words.en: A scenario is a description of a possible course of action or events.

words.ex: He will surrender when he sees the police.
words.ex_cn: 当他看到警察时，他会投降。
words.en: If you surrender, you stop fighting or resisting someone and agree that you have been beaten.

words.ex: I perceive a change in his mood.
words.ex_cn: 我察觉到他的情绪有变化。
words.en: If you perceive something, you see, notice, or realize it, especially when it is not obvious.

words.ex: He learned about sexual health in school.
words.ex_cn: 他在学校学习了性健康。
words.en: Relating to the instincts, physiological processes, and activities connected with physical attraction or intimate physical contact between individuals.

words.tr:
v. 嬉戏
n. 嬉戏；欢乐的活动
words.ex: The children were frolicking in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园里嬉戏。
words.en: If people or animals frolic, they play or move in a lively, happy way.

words.ex: She readily agreed to help me.
words.ex_cn: 她很容易就同意帮我了。
words.en: If you do something readily, you do it in a way which shows that you are very willing to do it.

words.ex: The change in her mood was observable.
words.ex_cn: 她情绪的变化是能察觉到的。
words.en: Something that is observable can be seen or noticed.

words.tr: v. 暂停；中止；延期； suspending
words.ex: The school will suspend the class due to snow.
words.ex_cn: 由于下雪，学校将暂停课程。
words.en: If you suspend something, you delay it or stop it from happening for a while or until a decision is made about it.

words.tr:
n. 叙述；叙事；
adj. 叙述性的；
words.ex: He told a simple narrative about his childhood.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了一个关于他童年的简单故事。
words.en: A narrative is a story or an account of a series of events.

words.tr: n. 魔鬼；恶魔；精力充沛的人；高手
words.ex: The child fears the demon in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 孩子害怕黑暗中的恶魔。
words.en: A demon is an evil spirit.

words.tr:
adj. 军事的；军用的；
n. 军队；武装力量；
words.ex: The military base is near the border.
words.ex_cn: 军事基地靠近边境。
words.en: relating to or characteristic of soldiers or armed forces

words.ex: Victor won the race last Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 维克多上周日赢得了比赛。
words.en: A victor is someone who wins a competition, battle, or game.

words.tr: adj. 无忧无虑的；轻松愉快的；
words.ex: The children played carefree in the park.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在公园里无忧无虑地玩耍。
words.en: If you are carefree, you have no worries or responsibilities, and you are happy and relaxed.

words.ex: He spoke with confidence during the presentation.
words.ex_cn: 他在演讲时充满信心。
words.en: Confidence is a feeling of self-assurance arising from one's appreciation of one's own abilities or qualities.

words.ex: I am awaiting the bus.
words.ex_cn: 我正在等公交车。
words.en: If you await someone or something, you wait for them.

words.ex: The city became prosperous after the new factory opened.
words.ex_cn: 新工厂开业后，这座城市变得繁荣了。
words.en: A prosperous person, place, or economy is rich and successful.

words.ex: The inventive child made a toy from cardboard.
words.ex_cn: 这个有创造力的孩子用纸板做了一个玩具。
words.en: If you describe someone as inventive, you mean that they are good at inventing things or have clever and original ideas.

words.ex: They live in a quiet suburb outside the city.
words.ex_cn: 他们住在城市外一个安静的市郊。
words.en: A suburb is a residential district located on the outskirts of a city.

words.ex: The loud music distract me from my homework.
words.ex_cn: 嘈杂的音乐让我无法专心做作业。
words.en: If something distracts you or your attention, it makes you stop concentrating on what you are doing.

words.tr: adj. 迷人的；有魅力的； v. “captivate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The captivating story made everyone silent.
words.ex_cn: 这个迷人的故事让所有人都沉默了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as captivating, you mean that they are fascinating and attractive.

chapters.name: The photo Phrases and expressions

words.tr: phrase. 处于危险中；冒风险；在电话线上；在线路上
words.ex: He is on the line when the phone rings.
words.ex_cn: 电话响时，他正在通话中。
words.en: At risk of being lost or harmed.

words.tr: phrase. 掌握某人的动向；了解某人的情况；与某人保持联系
words.ex: I keep track of my brother after school.
words.ex_cn: 我放学后一直留意我弟弟的行踪。
words.en: To keep informed about someone's activities or whereabouts.

words.ex: I keep track of my expenses every day.
words.ex_cn: 我每天记录我的开支。
words.en: To keep track of something means to stay informed about it or to record it, especially in order to notice any changes or developments.

words.ex: His behavior may border on rudeness.
words.ex_cn: 他的行为可能近乎无礼。
words.en: To be very close to something in quality, character, or nature, often suggesting that it almost reaches that state or condition.

words.w: out of the corner of one's eye
words.uk: /aʊt əv ðə ˈkɔːnə əv wʌnz aɪ/
words.us: /aʊt əv ðə ˈkɔːrnər əv wʌnz aɪ/
words.ex: I saw a cat out of the corner of my eye.
words.ex_cn: 我用余光看到了一只猫。
words.en: If you see something out of the corner of your eye, you see it but not clearly because it happens to the side of you.

words.tr: phrase. 引起共鸣；触动情感（尤指唤起熟悉或强烈的情感反应）
words.ex: The song strikes a chord with many people.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌引起了许多人的共鸣。
words.en: To cause someone to feel sympathy, emotion, or enthusiasm.

words.tr: phrase. 引起某人共鸣；触动某人的情感或记忆
words.ex: The song struck a chord with her because it reminded her of her childhood.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌触动了她，因为它让她想起了童年。
words.en: If something strikes a chord with you, it makes you feel sympathy or enthusiasm.

words.ex: He tried to gloss over his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他试图掩饰自己的错误。
words.en: To gloss over something means to treat or describe it in a way that fails to acknowledge its importance or complexity, often in order to avoid dealing with it directly.

words.tr: phrase. （某事）被某人接受或认同；（某事）合某人的心意
words.ex: His joke did not sit well with her.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话让她不舒服。
words.en: If something sits well with someone, it is acceptable to them or they are comfortable with it.

words.tr: phrase. 使某人感到不舒服；令某人难以接受；不被某人认可
words.ex: His joke did not sit well with the teacher.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话让老师不舒服。
words.en: If something does not sit well with someone, it does not fit in with their ideas or plans and they are not happy about it.

words.ex: He went for a walk regardless of the rain.
words.ex_cn: 尽管下雨，他还是去散步了。
words.en: Without taking into account; without being affected by.

chapters.name: The top five paintings in Western art New words

words.ex: There was an array of people at the concert.
words.ex_cn: 音乐会上人山人海。
words.en: An array of different things or people is a large number or wide range of them.

words.ex: The painting is considered a masterpiece by art critics.
words.ex_cn: 这幅画被艺术评论家视为杰作。
words.en: A masterpiece is a work of art such as a painting, film, or book that is made with great skill and is considered to be the best work of a particular artist or writer.

words.tr: adj. 令人沮丧的；令人泄气的；让人懊恼的； v. “frustrate”的现在分词；
words.ex: The slow internet is frustrating.
